html:
The capital of Nigeria, a planned city built in the centre of the country. The military government of Murtala Mohammed chose the site in 1976, and the seat of government moved there from Lagos in December 1991 under Ibrahim Babangida.

Lagos was crowded, on the coast, and in the Yoruba south. A capital in the middle of the country, on land not tied to any of the big ethnic groups, was meant to stand for national unity after the civil war. The city was laid out from scratch on a master plan, with the Japanese architect Kenzo Tange designing its central district. Its landmarks include the huge granite outcrop of Aso Rock, behind the presidential villa, and the National Mosque and the National Christian Centre.

Abuja is one of the fastest growing cities in Africa, and like Brasília, another planned inland capital, it has been surrounded by unplanned settlements that the plan did not foresee.
